findings.current: At my thoughtless mutter, the man gave a faint smile.
findings.defect: “Thoughtless” characterizes the remark as inconsiderate, while 무심코 means it slipped out unintentionally.
findings.rationale: The source describes an unconscious or accidental utterance, not a judgment about Taekyung’s consideration for others.
findings.replacement: At my inadvertent mutter, the man gave a faint smile.
findings.source: 무심코 흘러나온 내 중얼거림에 상대가 희미하게 웃었다.

findings.current: “Ah. Of course, I have a separate given name. However, I have been called Huginn ever since I began serving the Guild Master, so I believe you may call me that as well.”
findings.defect: 본명 means his real or legal name, not specifically his given name.
findings.rationale: The source contrasts Huginn with his 본명 without specifying whether that name is a personal, family, or full name.
findings.replacement: “Ah. Of course, I have another real name. However, I have been called Huginn ever since I began serving the Guild Master, so I believe you may call me that as well.”
findings.source: 아. 물론 본명은 따로 있습니다만, 길드장님을 모시게 된 후부터는 후긴이라 불리고 있으니 두 분께서도 그렇게 알아주시면 될 듯합니다.

findings.current: But more than twenty years ago, Cheon Taemin had vanished in front of everyone.
findings.defect: “Vanished in front of everyone” suggests that witnesses saw Cheon Taemin disappear, whereas 종적을 감추고 사라졌다 describes him disappearing from public view without a trace.
findings.rationale: The source concerns Cheon Taemin’s unexplained absence from society, not a witnessed act of instantaneous disappearance.
findings.replacement: But a little over twenty years ago, Cheon Taemin disappeared from the public eye without a trace.
findings.source: 하지만 지금으로부터 20여 년 전, 천태민이 모두의 앞에서 종적을 감추고 사라졌다.

findings.current: It felt like meeting an envoy from some superior kingdom.
findings.defect: “Superior kingdom” sounds like a qualitative compliment and loses the political hierarchy encoded by 상국, a dominant or suzerain state addressing a subordinate one.
findings.rationale: The metaphor specifically conveys Odin Guild treating Ares Guild as a subordinate power, which is central to Huginn’s condescension.
findings.replacement: It felt as though we were receiving an envoy from our suzerain.
findings.source: 꼭 상국(上國)의 사절을 만난 듯한 기분.

findings.current: It was an eternal truth that the higher a person’s position, the heavier their backside became.
findings.defect: The literal rendering is an unnatural English calque and obscures the idiom’s meaning that powerful people become increasingly reluctant to leave their seats or make personal appearances.
findings.rationale: This preserves both the physical seat-based joke and the explanation for why major Guild Masters avoid outside contact.
findings.replacement: The higher someone rose, the harder it became to pry them out of their seat. That was an eternal truth.
findings.source: 지위가 높은 사람일수록 엉덩이가 무거워지는 건 만고불변의 진리다.

findings.current: “Acquaintances he has known for many years. The person he was supposed to meet today was from Chronos… Ah, my apologies. I seem to have said something unnecessary.”
findings.defect: “Was supposed to meet” implies that the meeting may already have been missed or canceled. The source states that the person he is scheduled to meet today is from Chronos.
findings.rationale: The ongoing appointment supports Huginn’s deliberate implication that Odin’s Guild Master is currently coordinating with other major Guilds.
findings.replacement: “Acquaintances he has known for many years. The person he is scheduled to meet today is from Chronos… Ah, my apologies. I seem to have said something unnecessary.”
findings.source: 오늘 뵙기로 한 분은 크로노스의……. 아, 죄송합니다. 제가 괜한 말을 했군요.

findings.current:
Team Leader Choi shrugged at my question.

“Even so, isn’t this much better than talking around the subject several times, as you did a moment ago?”

“That’s true. If you’d said it like that again, I really would have…”
findings.defect: Both uses of “you” assign the earlier evasive speech to Taekyung or Choi. In the source, Choi and Taekyung are discussing Huginn’s earlier habit of talking in circles.
findings.rationale: The omitted Korean subject is resolved by the exchange: Huginn was the one who previously spoke indirectly, while Taekyung forced him to state his threat plainly.
findings.replacement:
Team Leader Choi shrugged at my question.

“Still, isn’t this much better than him talking in circles like he did a moment ago?”

“That’s true. If he’d kept talking like that this time, I really would have…”
findings.source:
내 물음에 최 팀장이 어깨를 으쓱했다.

“그래도 조금 전처럼 몇 바퀴 돌려서 말하는 것보다는 훨씬 낫지 않습니까.”

“그건 그래. 이번에도 아까처럼 말했으면 그땐 진짜…….”

findings.current: The unsettled feeling he had developed while dealing with Jin Taekyung seemed to fall back into place.
findings.defect: An “unsettled feeling” cannot naturally “fall back into place,” and the source refers to Huginn’s shaken composure or confidence returning to normal.
findings.rationale: 마음이 흔들렸다가 제자리를 찾다 describes his internal equilibrium being disturbed and then restored after he believes Choi has yielded.
findings.replacement: His composure, shaken by dealing with Jin Taekyung, seemed to settle back into place.
findings.source: 진태경을 상대하며 흔들렸던 마음이 제자리를 찾는 기분이다.

summary: Several actionable fidelity issues alter agency, chronology, hierarchy, or characterization, alongside localized terminology and natural-English problems.
